title: A Ember for the Oath Revisited
premise: Silas Fairweather, exiled storm-caller and reluctant charm-seller in the magic-free city of Vellamere, discovers his own name and tonight's date inked in a century-old book of prophecies. When the prophecy drags him and the archivist Wren Halloway into its unfolding, they learn the king has been hollowed out by a crown-bound entity that feeds on memory — the same entity that erased Silas's past and drove him into exile. To save the last dragon-fire from guttering out, Silas must choose between recovering his stolen memories and using that same fire to unbind the king. In the end he burns his memories willingly, freeing both king and dragon, and chooses to build new ones with Wren rather than mourn the old.
about_author: Rosalind Almeida is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing ship logs before turning to fiction full-time. She writes fantasy about people haunted by what they've forgotten, from a coastal cottage shared with too many cats and one opinionated lighthouse.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Silas sells a luck-charm to a nervous clerk while hiding the storm coiled under his skin, then meets Wren Halloway, an archivist who suspects his trinkets are more than brass and bone. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: weary loneliness cracked open by unexpected curiosity.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than Grief
chapters.summary: Wren shows Silas a prophetic ledger written a century ago; his name appears beside tonight's date, alongside hers. As they read aloud, the words pull them bodily into the archive's sealed vault, where the air tastes of ozone and old blood. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Escaping the vault, they witness King Aldous at a public rite — and Silas alone sees the thing behind his eyes, a memory-eater wearing royalty like a glove. The entity notices Silas seeing it. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: recognition and terror, for the entity is what erased him.

chapters.title: Five Years of Borrowed Sky
chapters.summary: Hunted through Vellamere's rain-slick streets, Silas confesses his exile: he was a royal storm-caller whose memories were devoured as punishment. Wren realizes the prophecy needs them both alive until the final line. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: trust forged in confession.

chapters.title: The Dragon Beneath the City
chapters.summary: Following the ledger's marginalia, they find the last dragon, Emberveil, chained beneath the palace, her fire the only thing keeping the crown-entity anchored to the mortal plane. She offers Silas a terrible bargain. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: awe curdling into moral weight.

chapters.title: A Traitor's Kindness
chapters.summary: Silas's old mentor, Captain Ives, betrays their location to the crown — but slips Wren a key, revealing he sold them out only to buy time against the entity's purge of the archives. POV: Ives. Emotional beat: guilt and love entangled.

chapters.title: Ash in the Ledger
chapters.summary: The entity burns the prophecy's remaining pages, hoping to unwrite its foretold defeat; Wren recites the lost lines from memory, bleeding power she doesn't understand. The city's outlawed magic stirs awake. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: sacrifice without certainty.

chapters.title: The Hollow King Speaks
chapters.summary: Captured and brought before Aldous, Silas bargains with the entity directly: it offers his memories back if he abandons Wren and Emberveil. He sees, briefly, the boy he was. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: temptation at its most human.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Iron Throne
chapters.summary: Climax: Silas calls the storm he swore off, shattering the throne room while Wren frees Emberveil. To unbind the king, Silas must feed his recovered memories to the dragon-fire — erasing himself to end the entity. He does it. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into choice.

chapters.title: New Ink, Same Hand
chapters.summary: The king wakes hollow but free; Emberveil rises skyward, her fire no longer a chain. Silas remembers nothing of his old life but keeps the feeling of having chosen rightly. Wren begins writing a new ledger — starting with his name. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: quiet hope, identity rebuilt from love.
